subject: Moon-forming impact
caption: A Moon-sized body smashes into a rocky planet in a NASA artist's concept, the kind of giant collision thought to have made our Moon.
note: Painted to show a collision seen around the star HD 172555, not the Earth itself. It is a stand-in for the Theia impact, whose details are still debated.

subject: Early molten Earth
caption: An artist's view of the young Earth's surface, with lava flows, falling meteors and a huge Moon hanging close overhead.
note: Artistic impression. The Moon really was much closer then, but nobody knows what the surface looked like, and newer work suggests oceans may have formed early in the Hadean.

subject: Archean banded chert, Pilbara
caption: Red and white banded chert at Marble Bar in Western Australia, sea-floor rock laid down about 3.4 billion years ago.
note: A sandal is in the corner of the photo for scale.
imageDateLabel: Rock formed about 3.4 billion years ago

subject: Stromatolite, about 3.4 billion years old
caption: A cut slice of layered rock from the Pilbara of Western Australia, about 3.4 billion years old, with wavy layers thought to have been built by mats of microbes.
note: Most researchers accept the Strelley Pool stromatolites as made by life, but for rocks this old a non-living origin is still argued by some.
imageDateLabel: Rock formed about 3.4 billion years ago

subject: Acasta Gneiss, the oldest known rock
caption: A piece of the Acasta Gneiss from northern Canada, about 4.03 billion years old and the oldest known rock that is still part of the Earth's crust.
note: Its age marks the boundary between the Hadean and the Archean, so it could sit under either unit.
imageDateLabel: Rock formed about 4.03 billion years ago

subject: Banded iron formation
caption: Red and grey striped banded iron formation at Dales Gorge in Western Australia, iron that rusted out of the sea about 2.5 billion years ago as oxygen first built up.
note: These Hamersley rocks are about 2.5 billion years old, right at the Archean to Proterozoic boundary.
imageDateLabel: Rock formed about 2.5 billion years ago

subject: Stromatolites
caption: Living stromatolites at Hamelin Pool, Shark Bay, Western Australia: rocky mounds built layer by layer by microbes, just as they were billions of years ago.
note: A photo of modern stromatolites, a few thousand years old, used to show what the Precambrian shallows looked like.

subject: Proterozoic stromatolite
caption: A polished slice through fossil stromatolites about 1.4 billion years old from Montana, showing the fine layers laid down by microbial mats.

subject: Stromatolites
caption: A wide view of living stromatolites along the shore of Hamelin Pool in Shark Bay, Western Australia.
note: Modern stromatolites, shown as a living example of the microbe-built mounds that dominated Precambrian coasts.

subject: Snowball Earth
caption: An artist's view of the Earth from space almost wholly covered in ice during an ancient global glaciation.
note: Drawn for the Huronian glaciation of about 2.4 to 2.1 billion years ago. How completely the Earth froze, then and in the later Cryogenian snowballs, is still debated.

subject: Dickinsonia
caption: A fossil of Dickinsonia costata, a flat, ribbed oval that is one of the oldest known animals, pressed into sandstone about 555 million years ago.

subject: Ediacaran sea floor
caption: A museum model of the Ediacaran sea floor with tall frond-like Charnia and flat, ribbed Dickinsonia lying on the sand.
note: Colours are invented, and what kind of creatures the fronds were is still uncertain.

subject: Fractofusus, Mistaken Point
caption: A digital reconstruction of Fractofusus, a spindle-shaped Ediacaran organism, lying on a dark sea floor about 570 million years ago with smaller young around it.
note: The threads linking the individuals follow a published idea about how it reproduced; colour and texture are guesses.

subject: Anomalocaris
caption: A nearly complete Anomalocaris canadensis fossil from the Burgess Shale of Canada, about 505 million years old, showing the body flaps and tail fan.
note: Portrait format.

subject: Hallucigenia
caption: A detailed digital reconstruction of Hallucigenia, a tiny spiny worm with legs, climbing on a sponge in the dark Cambrian sea.
note: Shown the right way up and the right way round, following the 2015 study that found its head. Portrait format, with a small artist signature.

subject: Anomalocaris
caption: A clean modern reconstruction of Anomalocaris canadensis on a white background, with its two spiny grasping arms, stalked eyes and swimming flaps.
note: Has a small artist signature in the corner.

subject: Anomalocaris
caption: Anomalocaris, the top hunter of the Cambrian seas, chases shelled Isoxys through sunlit blue water.
note: Colours are invented. Recent studies suggest Anomalocaris chased soft, fast prey in open water, as shown here, instead of crushing trilobites.

subject: Cambrian sea life
caption: A busy Cambrian sea floor in what is now North China about 504 million years ago, with swimming radiodonts, trilobites, sponges and jellyfish.
note: Based on the Linyi fossil site and published in a scientific paper; drawing by Dinghua Yang. The original is 1269 px wide.

subject: Trilobite (Olenoides)
caption: A Burgess Shale trilobite, Olenoides serratus, preserved with its legs and antennae as well as its hard shell.
note: Portrait format.

subject: Opabinia
caption: A reconstruction of Opabinia regalis on a white background, with five eyes on stalks and a long trunk ending in a claw.
note: Has a small artist signature in the corner.

subject: Opabinia
caption: Two Opabinia search the Cambrian sea floor among sponges, using their clawed trunks to grab food.
note: Colours are invented.

subject: Ordovician sea (Fezouata)
caption: The Early Ordovician sea of Morocco, with the two-metre filter-feeding giant Aegirocassis gliding over a sea floor crowded with trilobites and other arthropods.
note: Based on the Fezouata fossil beds, about 478 million years old. Colours are invented.

subject: Sea scorpion (Pentecopterus)
caption: Pentecopterus, a sea scorpion nearly as long as a person, hunts over rippled sand 467 million years ago.
note: The oldest known sea scorpion. Colours are invented.

subject: Ordovician sea floor
caption: A museum model of a Late Ordovician sea floor with a straight-shelled nautiloid, a large trilobite, sea lilies, corals and shells.
note: An older style museum diorama; the bright colours are guesses and the seaweeds are stand-ins.

subject: Silurian sea floor (Herefordshire)
caption: A dark Silurian sea floor about 430 million years ago, crowded with small arthropods, worms and a shelled brachiopod, all known from fossils found in Herefordshire, England.
note: The animals are only a few millimetres to centimetres long in life. Colours are invented.

subject: Cooksonia, an early land plant
caption: A museum model of Cooksonia, an early land plant with leafless forked stems and spore capsules at their tips.
note: Shown ten times life size.

subject: Sea scorpion (Eurypterus)
caption: A complete fossil of the sea scorpion Eurypterus remipes from New York State, with its swimming paddles and tail spine.

subject: Sea scorpion (Eurypterus)
caption: Three Eurypterus sea scorpions swim over a sandy bottom in clear blue water, paddling with their broad back legs.
note: A digital model placed on a modern underwater photograph.

subject: Dunkleosteus
caption: The armoured skull of Dunkleosteus terrelli, with self-sharpening bony blades in place of teeth.
note: A museum cast of the original fossil.

subject: Dunkleosteus
caption: Three species of the armoured fish Dunkleosteus drawn to scale, with the bladed jaws and bony head shield of the largest, D. terrelli, at the top.
note: Follows the 2023 rethink that made Dunkleosteus shorter and deeper bodied (about 4 m) than older 6 to 9 m pictures. Species labels and a scale bar are part of the image.

subject: Devonian river life (Hyneria)
caption: Hyneria, a lobe-finned fish up to three metres long, swims through a weedy Late Devonian river past smaller fish.
note: Painted in 2015; the body shape is partly guessed, as Hyneria is known from incomplete remains.

subject: Tiktaalik
caption: The front half of a Tiktaalik fossil from Arctic Canada, showing the flat, crocodile-like skull, the neck and the scaly body.
credit: Matt Mechtley from Tempe, Arizona, USA

subject: Tiktaalik
caption: Tiktaalik, a fish with a flat head, a neck and sturdy front fins, props itself up at the water's edge about 375 million years ago.
note: Made in 2006. Later finds showed Tiktaalik also had a large pelvis and strong hind fins.

subject: Trilobite (Walliserops)
caption: A Devonian trilobite from Morocco, Walliserops trifurcatus, with a long three-pronged fork on its head and rows of spines.

subject: Arthropleura
caption: Arthropleura, a millipede relative more than two metres long, walks along a sandy shore, leaving a trackway behind it.
note: Has a small artist signature in the corner. Colour is a guess.

subject: Carboniferous coal forest
caption: A large early four-legged animal lies among ferns at the foot of giant scale trees in a museum reconstruction of a coal swamp.
note: Photograph of a museum diorama.

subject: Carboniferous coal forest
caption: A museum reconstruction of a coal swamp 310 million years ago, with giant horsetails and scale trees standing over misty water.
note: Photograph of a museum diorama.

subject: Meganeura
caption: A life-size model of Meganeura, a dragonfly-like insect with a wingspan of about 70 cm, resting on the trunk of a scale tree.
note: Photograph of a museum model.

subject: Dimetrodon
caption: A detailed 3D model of Dimetrodon, the sail-backed hunter of the early Permian, standing with its legs held fairly upright.
note: Dimetrodon was not a dinosaur but an early relative of mammals. Skin and colour are informed guesses.

subject: Dimetrodon
caption: A mounted Dimetrodon skeleton from Texas against a black background, showing the tall spines that held up its sail.

subject: Dimetrodon
caption: Dimetrodon grandis in side view on a white background, walking with its belly off the ground and the tips of its sail spines bare.
note: The name and dates are written on the image.

subject: Giant griffinfly fossil (Arctotypus)
caption: The imprint of a giant griffinfly with a 68 cm wingspan, a close relative of Meganeura, preserved in dark Permian slate from France.
note: The file name says Meganeura monyi, but the Commons description identifies the specimen as Arctotypus intermedius, a Permian relative.

subject: Helicoprion
caption: Helicoprion, a Permian relative of ratfish with a spiral saw of teeth set in its lower jaw.
note: Only the tooth spirals and some jaw cartilage are known, so the body is modelled on relatives.

subject: Gorgonopsian (Inostrancevia)
caption: Inostrancevia, a sabre-toothed gorgonopsian and top predator at the very end of the Permian, drawn on a white background.
note: Colour is a guess; whether gorgonopsians had hair is not known.

subject: Permian lakeshore, South Africa
caption: A middle Permian lakeshore in South Africa, with Glossopteris trees, horsetails and early mammal relatives at the water's edge.
note: From a 2022 scientific paper; three round inset panels with letters are part of the image.

subject: Scutosaurus
caption: Scutosaurus, a bulky, armour-skinned plant eater of the late Permian of Russia, shown on a white background.
credit: Marco Romano, Fabio Manucci, Bruce Rubidge and Marc J. Van den Brandt
note: From a 2021 scientific paper that built the body around a real skeleton.

subject: Herrerasaurus
caption: Herrerasaurus, one of the earliest known meat-eating dinosaurs, from Argentina about 231 million years ago, on a plain white background.
note: Colour and pattern are guesses.

subject: Morganucodon
caption: Morganucodon, a shrew-sized early relative of mammals that lived alongside the first dinosaurs.
note: Lived about 205 million years ago, across the Triassic to Jurassic boundary. Fur colour is a guess.

subject: Early Triassic river landscape
caption: A river plain in Australia a few million years after the end-Permian extinction, with spiky Pleuromeia plants, seed ferns, a reptile on the bank and an amphibian in the shallows.
note: Portrait format (taller than wide).

subject: Early dinosaurs (coelophysids)
caption: Slender early meat-eating dinosaurs walk through a Late Triassic landscape of conifers and ferns while small pterosaurs fly overhead.
note: Photograph of a traditional painting. The dinosaurs are generic coelophysids shown with the Italian pterosaur Peteinosaurus.

subject: Triassic riverbank with Prestosuchus
caption: A giant crocodile-line predator, Prestosuchus, feeds on a dicynodont beside a river in Brazil about 237 million years ago, while small Parvosuchus scavenge.
note: Shows a bloody carcass. Based on the Santa Maria Formation of Brazil (Middle to Late Triassic), a world still ruled by crocodile relatives rather than dinosaurs.

subject: Coelophysis
caption: Coelophysis, a light, fast early dinosaur from the Late Triassic of North America, drawn for the US National Park Service.
note: The thin fuzzy coat and the bright colours are speculative; no skin or feathers are known for Coelophysis.

subject: Herrerasaurus and Eoraptor skeletons
caption: Museum skeletons of two of the earliest dinosaurs, large Herrerasaurus and small Eoraptor, with a Plateosaurus skull, in a display on dinosaur origins.
note: Casts behind glass with a light reflection on the case. No good openly licensed life reconstruction of Eoraptor was found.

subject: Lystrosaurus
caption: Lystrosaurus, a pig-sized tusked plant-eater that survived the end-Permian extinction and spread across the Early Triassic world.
note: Coloured-pencil drawing. Skin covering and colour are not known from fossils.

subject: Lystrosaurus and its predator Moschorhinus
caption: The predator Moschorhinus stands over a Lystrosaurus it has killed in South Africa around the time of the end-Permian extinction.
note: Fur and whiskers on the predator are speculative. Shows a wound on the prey.

subject: Archaeopteryx (Berlin specimen)
caption: The Berlin specimen of Archaeopteryx, found in Bavarian limestone, with clear feather impressions around its wings and tail.
note: Portrait format (taller than wide).

subject: Sauropods (Europasaurus) on a Jurassic island
caption: Europasaurus sauropods cross a beach beside tall conifer forest on a Late Jurassic island in what is now Germany, with iguanodont dinosaurs and pterosaurs around them.
note: Europasaurus was a dwarf island sauropod only about 6 metres long, not a giant like Brachiosaurus.

subject: Sauropod herds of the Morrison Formation
caption: Herds of several kinds of long-necked diplodocid sauropods gather at a Late Jurassic waterhole at sunset.
credit: Pedro Salas and Sergey Krasovskiy, with others

subject: Ammonite (Dactylioceras)
caption: Dactylioceras commune, a ribbed ammonite from the Early Jurassic of England, photographed on a white background.

subject: Archaeopteryx
caption: A black-feathered Archaeopteryx chases a young Compsognathus through a Late Jurassic forest in what is now Germany.
note: The black wing colour follows a pigment study of a single fossil feather; whole-body colour and this hunting behaviour are guesses.

subject: Brachiosaurus
caption: Brachiosaurus, a giant sauropod with a giraffe-like upright neck and long front legs, on a plain white background.
note: Colours and skin pattern are guesses.

subject: Diplodocus
caption: Diplodocus, a 25-metre long-necked sauropod with a whip-like tail, on a plain white background.
note: The row of small spines along the back is based on skin fossils of a related diplodocid. Colours are guesses.

subject: Ichthyosaur fossil (Stenopterygius)
caption: Fossil of the ichthyosaur Stenopterygius from Holzmaden, Germany, preserved with the dark outline of its skin, back fin and tail, with a young one beside it.
note: On some Holzmaden specimens the body outline was touched up by preparators. A museum label is visible in the lower left corner.

subject: Ichthyosaur (Temnodontosaurus)
caption: The giant ichthyosaur Temnodontosaurus seizes a smaller ichthyosaur, Stenopterygius, in an Early Jurassic sea.

subject: Early Jurassic forest scene
caption: A large meat-eating dinosaur, early sauropods and small theropods in an Early Jurassic forest of conifers, cycads and ferns in what is now Poland.
note: Many of the animals are known there only from footprints or fragments. The artist's signature and date are painted into the lower left corner.

subject: Morrison Formation panorama
caption: A panoramic mural of the Late Jurassic Morrison floodplain of western North America, with Allosaurus, long-necked sauropods and Stegosaurus along a river.
credit: National Park Service / Bob Walters and Tess Kissinger
note: Extremely wide panorama (about 4.3 to 1); the original is 23,847 px wide.

subject: Allosaurus and Ceratosaurus
caption: Allosaurus and Ceratosaurus squabble over dried-out carcasses during a drought in the Late Jurassic of Colorado.
note: Dark and gory. A small artist credit line with a web address sits in the lower right corner. Illustrates a 2020 study of bite marks, including possible cannibalism.

subject: Pliosaur (Liopleurodon)
caption: Liopleurodon, a short-necked pliosaur and top predator of Middle to Late Jurassic seas, swims just under the surface.

subject: Plesiosaur (Plesiosaurus)
caption: Two long-necked Plesiosaurus hunt fish in a sunlit Early Jurassic sea.
note: Drawn in 2007. Newer research suggests plesiosaurs had a small tail fin and a stiffer neck than shown.

subject: Pterosaur (Rhamphorhynchus)
caption: A flock of long-tailed Rhamphorhynchus pterosaurs skims over a Late Jurassic sea.
note: 3D render in a very wide banner format (3 to 1).

subject: Stegosaurus
caption: Stegosaurus, with two rows of large plates along its back and four spikes on its tail, on a plain white background.
note: Plate colours are guesses.

subject: Late Cretaceous Alberta panorama
caption: Horned dinosaurs, armoured dinosaurs and duck-bills in a sunlit forest clearing in Late Cretaceous Alberta, about 75 million years ago.
note: Very wide panorama (3.4 to 1); the original is 2758 px wide.

subject: Pterosaurs of Late Cretaceous Mongolia
caption: Giant azhdarchid pterosaurs fly, squabble and catch small prey beside a lake in Late Cretaceous Mongolia while duck-billed dinosaurs drink.
note: From a 2025 paper naming new pterosaur species from fragmentary bones; crest shapes and colours are guesses.

subject: Arctic dinosaurs of Alaska
caption: Feathered dromaeosaurs, horned Pachyrhinosaurus and tiny mammals under the northern lights in the polar forest of Late Cretaceous Alaska.
credit: Andrey Atuchin from Chiarenza et al. 2020
note: The dromaeosaur is known there only from a jaw fragment and teeth, so its appearance is based on relatives.

subject: Mosasaur (Tylosaurus)
caption: The mosasaur Tylosaurus lunges at a short-necked plesiosaur in the Late Cretaceous inland sea of North America.
credit: Andrey Atuchin in Zietlow et al.
note: Commons marks this file as awaiting licence review; it is credited to a CC BY 4.0 paper (Zietlow et al.).

subject: Pterosaur (Pteranodon) seized by a shark
caption: The shark Cretoxyrhina leaps from the Late Cretaceous inland sea of North America with a Pteranodon in its jaws.
note: Based on a Pteranodon neck bone with a shark tooth stuck in it; whether the shark hunted or scavenged is not known.

subject: Tyrannosaurus rex (Sue)
caption: Sue, one of the largest and most complete Tyrannosaurus rex skeletons, on display at the Field Museum in Chicago.
note: The skull on the mount is a cast; the real skull is displayed separately.

subject: Ammonite with iridescent shell
caption: A fossil ammonite whose mother-of-pearl shell still shimmers with rainbow colours, on display at the American Museum of Natural History.
note: The species and age are not given on the file page; ammonites preserved like this usually come from the Late Cretaceous of North America.

subject: Chicxulub impact
caption: A NASA painting of the asteroid striking the shallow sea at Chicxulub, Mexico, 66 million years ago.
note: Commons tags this as inaccurate paleoart: the pterosaurs look like Pteranodon, which had died out millions of years earlier, and are drawn in an outdated style. The impact itself is an artist's impression.

subject: Mid-Cretaceous river scene
caption: Plant-eating dinosaurs, an armoured nodosaur, a small raptor and a crocodile relative at a forest river in mid-Cretaceous Colorado, with fresh footprints in the mud.
note: Painted for the US National Park Service from footprints and bones found in the area.

subject: Feathered dinosaur (Deinonychus)
caption: Deinonychus, a wolf-sized raptor with a large sickle claw on each foot, shown fully feathered on a plain white background.
note: Feathers are inferred from close relatives; none are preserved with Deinonychus itself.

subject: Feathered dinosaur (Microraptor)
caption: Microraptor, a crow-sized dinosaur with flight feathers on both its arms and its legs, gliding on a plain white background.
note: The glossy black colour follows a 2012 pigment study. How it held its hind wings in the air is debated.

subject: Pterosaur (Quetzalcoatlus)
caption: Giraffe-sized Quetzalcoatlus pterosaurs walk on all fours across a fern prairie and one snatches a baby sauropod.
note: Painted in 2008; later studies have revised the head and crest shape.

subject: Sinosauropteryx fossil
caption: Fossil of Sinosauropteryx from China, the first dinosaur found with a coat of simple feathers, seen as a dark fringe along its back and tail.
credit: Sam / Olai Ose / Skjaervoy from Zhangjiagang, China

subject: Triceratops skeleton
caption: Mounted Triceratops skeleton from the Natural History Museum of Los Angeles County, cut out on a white background.
note: The museum background has been removed digitally.

subject: Feathered dinosaur (Zhenyuanlong)
caption: Zhenyuanlong, a relative of Velociraptor from China whose fossil preserves large bird-like wing and tail feathers.
note: Feather shapes come from the fossil; colours are guesses.

subject: Chicxulub crater today
caption: Radar and satellite views of the Yucatan Peninsula in Mexico, where a faint curved trough marks the buried rim of the Chicxulub crater.
note: Two stacked images in portrait format. The crater is buried under younger rock and shows only faintly.

subject: Tyrannosaurus rex in the Hell Creek swamp
caption: Tyrannosaurus rex wades through a swamp forest with duck-billed Edmontosaurus, dome-headed Pachycephalosaurus and a feathered dromaeosaur.
note: Photograph of a traditional painting. Dakotaraptor, the feathered animal, is based on disputed fossil material.

subject: Cretaceous-Paleogene boundary clay
caption: The thin grey clay layer at Stevns Klint, Denmark, that marks the asteroid impact, lying between white Cretaceous chalk below and younger limestone above.

subject: Mosasaur (Mosasaurus)
caption: Mosasaurus hoffmannii, one of the largest mosasaurs, carries prey in its jaws over a shallow Late Cretaceous sea floor, with ammonites and a shark nearby.
note: Simple digital style in a wide banner format.

subject: Early mammal (Repenomamus) attacking a dinosaur
caption: Pencil drawing of the badger-sized mammal Repenomamus biting the dinosaur Psittacosaurus, as the two were found locked together in a fossil from China.
note: Black and white drawing. Whether the fossil records a real attack was questioned when it was published in 2023.

subject: Triceratops
caption: Triceratops, the three-horned plant-eater with a bony neck frill, in side view on a plain white background.
note: Colours are guesses.

subject: Tyrannosaurus rex
caption: A heavily built Tyrannosaurus rex seen from the front and side, painted by palaeontologist and artist Mark Witton.
note: Loose painterly style. Colours are guesses.

subject: Feathered dinosaur (Yutyrannus)
caption: Yutyrannus, a 9-metre early relative of T. rex from China that was covered in long, simple feathers.
note: Filament feathers are preserved in the fossils; the colour is a guess.

subject: Paleocene rocks
caption: Badlands in North Dakota cut into mud and sand laid down by rivers and swamps in the Paleocene, soon after the dinosaurs died out.
note: A modern landscape photograph: the rocks are Paleocene (Fort Union Group), the scenery is today's.

subject: Pantolambda
caption: Pantolambda, a sheep-sized plant eater and one of the first large mammals to appear after the dinosaurs.
note: Fur colour and pattern are guesses.

subject: Eocene rainforest
caption: A hot, wet Eocene forest in what is now Oregon, with palms, banana plants, a crocodile and early hoofed mammals.
note: Based on the plant and animal fossils of the Clarno Nut Beds (about 44 million years old). Very wide panorama.

subject: Darwinius ('Ida')
caption: 'Ida', a 47-million-year-old early primate from the Messel Pit in Germany, preserved with the outline of her fur.
note: Once promoted as a human ancestor; most researchers now place Darwinius closer to lemurs than to monkeys and apes.

subject: Early whale (Basilosaurus / Dorudon)
caption: The backbone and ribs of an early whale lie in the Egyptian desert at Wadi al-Hitan, once the floor of a shallow sea.
note: The file does not say which whale this is; Basilosaurus and Dorudon skeletons are both found here, about 37 to 40 million years old.

subject: Early whale (Basilosaurus)
caption: Basilosaurus, an early whale about 15 to 18 metres long with a long eel-like body, swimming under the surface.
note: Skin colour and the exact body outline are guesses; the tail fluke is inferred from the tail bones.

subject: Early horse (Propalaeotherium)
caption: The complete skeleton of a fox-sized early horse relative from the Messel Pit in Germany, about 47 million years old.
note: Propalaeotherium is a close European relative of the first horses (Eohippus), not Eohippus itself.

subject: Early whale (Pakicetus)
caption: Pakicetus, a wolf-sized four-legged animal from about 50 million years ago and one of the earliest known relatives of whales.
note: Fur and colour are guesses; how much time it spent in water is still discussed.

subject: Early horse (Orohippus) and Uintatherium
caption: Small early horses run from the water's edge as two horned Uintatherium come to drink in a warm Eocene forest.
note: Painted in 1931 by Charles R. Knight. Still broadly reasonable, but the animals' build and the plants follow the knowledge of that time.

subject: Early whale (Ambulocetus)
caption: A cast skeleton and a life model of Ambulocetus, the 'walking whale' that could move on land and swim.
note: Museum display in Pisa: the skeleton is a restored cast and the model is an older, rather crocodile-like interpretation.

subject: Early horse (Sifrhippus / Eohippus)
caption: Sifrhippus, one of the very first horses, was about the size of a small dog and had several toes on each foot.
note: The spotted coat is a guess, modelled on small forest animals of today. The artist's signature is on the picture.

subject: Oligocene rocks (Badlands)
caption: The striped hills of Badlands National Park, South Dakota, built from mud and ash that buried Eocene and Oligocene animals.
note: A modern landscape photograph: the rock layers are about 37 to 28 million years old.

subject: Paraceratherium
caption: Two Paraceratherium, hornless rhinoceros relatives and among the largest land mammals ever, tower over a pair of Hyaenodon.
note: Known from incomplete skeletons, so the exact size, neck length and skin are estimates.

subject: Oligocene woodland
caption: Three-toed horses, early dogs, a tortoise and a cat-like nimravid in an open Oligocene woodland in Oregon, about 30 million years ago.
credit: Bureau of Land Management Oregon and Washington
note: Mural by Roger Witter for the John Day Fossil Beds, based on the fossils of the Turtle Cove beds. Commons marks it public domain as a US government work.

subject: Arsinoitherium
caption: Arsinoitherium, a rhinoceros-sized plant eater from Egypt with a pair of huge bony horns.
note: Pencil drawing by Mauricio Antón. It looks like a rhinoceros but was more closely related to elephants.

subject: Megalodon
caption: A megalodon, the largest shark known, bursts from the sea among small whales and seabirds.
note: Megalodon is known almost only from teeth and a few backbones, so its body shape is an estimate; this picture models it on a great white shark, which newer studies suggest may be too stocky. The artist's signature is in the corner.

subject: Ashfall Fossil Beds rhinoceroses
caption: Skeletons of barrel-bodied rhinoceroses lie where they died at a waterhole in Nebraska, buried by volcanic ash about 12 million years ago.
note: The red numbered discs are excavation markers.

subject: Megalodon
caption: Rebuilt jaws of megalodon set with real fossil teeth, hanging in the American Museum of Natural History.
note: Only the teeth are fossils. The jaw is a model, because shark skeletons are made of cartilage and rarely fossilise.

subject: Miocene landscape
caption: A warm late Miocene landscape in central Europe, with an elephant relative, a hornless rhinoceros and clawed chalicotheres.
note: A 2026 reconstruction published in a scientific paper; it combines animals and plants known from fossils into one imagined view.

subject: Miocene grassland
caption: Giant pig-like Daeodon, clawed Moropus, small rhinoceroses, camels and three-toed horses on the Miocene plains of North America.
note: Painted by Charles R. Knight about 1929 for the Field Museum. Still broadly reasonable, though details of the animals follow the knowledge of that time.

subject: Terror bird (Phorusrhacos)
caption: Phorusrhacos, a flightless hunting 'terror bird' about 2.5 metres tall that lived in South America.
note: Feather colours and the bare red face are guesses.

subject: Australopithecus afarensis ('Lucy')
caption: A digital reconstruction of the face of Lucy's species, Australopithecus afarensis.
note: Lucy's own skull is very incomplete, so a face like this leans on other skulls of her species. Skin, hair and eye colour cannot be known from fossils.

subject: Australopithecus afarensis ('Lucy')
caption: The bones of 'Lucy', a 3.2-million-year-old Australopithecus afarensis from Ethiopia who walked upright.
note: This is a cast in the Paris natural history museum; the original bones are kept in Addis Ababa. Tall, narrow picture.

subject: Pliocene landscape
caption: A Pliocene river landscape in central Europe, with mastodon-like elephants, a rhinoceros, tapirs and deer.
note: A 2026 reconstruction published in a scientific paper; it combines animals and plants known from fossils into one imagined view.

subject: Laetoli footprints
caption: Footprints left in wet volcanic ash at Laetoli, Tanzania, about 3.66 million years ago by upright-walking human relatives.
note: A museum cast in Vienna, not the original trackway, which is reburied in Tanzania to protect it.

subject: Ice Age animals
caption: Woolly mammoths, wild horses, a woolly rhinoceros and cave lions on a snowy plain in northern Spain during the last Ice Age.
note: Painting by Mauricio Antón, published in the open-access journal PLoS Biology.

subject: Neanderthal
caption: A life-size reconstruction of an older Neanderthal man holding a wooden spear, from the Neanderthal Museum in Germany.
note: Model by the Kennis brothers. The bone structure follows real skulls; skin tone, hair and expression are informed guesses. Tall picture.

subject: Woolly mammoth
caption: A life-size model of a woolly mammoth at the Royal British Columbia Museum.
note: A museum model; hair length and colour are based on frozen mammoths found in Siberia.

subject: Diprotodon
caption: A Diprotodon skeleton built from bones found at Lake Callabonna, South Australia.
note: A composite: the bones come from several animals.

subject: Glyptodon
caption: Glyptodon, a car-sized relative of armadillos with a domed shell made of hundreds of bony plates.
note: Colour is a guess.

subject: Glyptodon and relatives
caption: Three kinds of giant armoured glyptodonts on the grasslands of Ice Age South America, one with a spiked club on its tail.
note: Shows Glyptodon, Doedicurus and Panochthus together; colours are guesses.

subject: Sabre-toothed cat (Smilodon) at La Brea
caption: Sabre-toothed cats and giant vultures gather round animals trapped in the sticky tar pools of La Brea, California.
note: Mural by Charles R. Knight, about 1931. The cats look rather lion-like by today's standards, but the scene is still broadly reasonable.

subject: Ice Age steppe
caption: Central Europe in the last Ice Age: a cold open grassland with mammoths, woolly rhinoceros, bison and saiga antelope.
note: A 2026 reconstruction published in a scientific paper; it combines animals and plants known from fossils into one imagined view.

subject: Giant ground sloth (Megatherium)
caption: The skeleton of Megatherium, a giant ground sloth, rearing up against a tree trunk in the Natural History Museum, London.
note: The London skeleton is a plaster cast, not original bone.

subject: Neanderthal
caption: The face of a Neanderthal man, reconstructed for the Natural History Museum in London.
note: Model by the Kennis brothers. Skin, hair and the headband are informed guesses. Tall picture.

subject: Neanderthal
caption: The skull of the 'Old Man' of La Chapelle-aux-Saints, a Neanderthal who lived in France about 50,000 to 60,000 years ago.
note: The background has been replaced with a grey fade.

subject: Sabre-toothed cat (Smilodon)
caption: Smilodon fatalis, the sabre-toothed cat of Ice Age North America, with a heavy body and a short tail.
note: The spotted coat is a guess; fossils do not preserve fur colour.

subject: Woolly mammoth
caption: A herd of woolly mammoths crosses a snowy valley, with woolly rhinoceroses in the distance.
note: Mural by Charles R. Knight, about 1929. It still looks reasonable, though mammoths probably lived more on dry grassland than in deep snow.

subject: Diprotodon
caption: Diprotodon, a wombat relative the size of a rhinoceros and the largest marsupial that ever lived, grazing in Ice Age Australia.
note: Illustration by palaeontologist Nellie Pease. Fur and nose shape are guesses. Square picture with a soft white edge.

subject: Glacier ice
caption: The front of the Perito Moreno Glacier in Patagonia: a living reminder of the ice that covered far more of the world until about 12,000 years ago.
note: A modern photograph standing in for the Ice Age world; this glacier is not a leftover of the great ice sheets.

subject: Giant deer (Irish elk)
caption: The skull and antlers of a giant deer, whose antlers spanned up to 3.6 metres.
note: Mainly an Ice Age animal, placed here because it outlived the ice: the last giant deer lived in Siberia about 7,700 years ago.

subject: Moa and Haast's eagle
caption: A giant Haast's eagle attacks moa in New Zealand, where huge birds lived until people arrived about 700 years ago.
note: Painting by John Megahan (2004), published in the open-access journal PLoS Biology. Feather colours are guesses.

subject: Muskox
caption: Muskoxen in Alaska: shaggy survivors of the Ice Age that once lived alongside woolly mammoths.
note: A modern wildlife photograph.

subject: Tundra (Wrangel Island)
caption: Tundra on Wrangel Island in the Arctic Ocean, where the last woolly mammoths survived until about 4,000 years ago.
note: A modern photograph (2006), fittingly taken on the Mamontovaya, or Mammoth, River.
